speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the nature of the bleeding from your wisdom tooth extraction and share any details about your history of easy bruising. Also, have you experienced excessive bleeding during previous dental procedures or surgeries?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any joint swelling, nosebleeds, or bleeding after minor cuts in your life prior to this extraction? REQUEST TEST: PT/PTT, Platelet_Count, Fibrinogen. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI of affected joints if joint swelling is present.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Prothrombin_Time: 15 sec, Partial_Thromboplastin_Time: 60 sec, Platelet_Count: 160,000/mm3, Fibrinogen: Not Available in data, Joint Swelling: No active joint swelling observed

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency).

Based on your severe bleeding post-extraction, easy bruising, family history of joint swelling, and the absence of platelet abnormalities in the initial workup, this clinical picture is classic for an X-linked bleeding disorder affecting clotting factors. While a specific factor assay (Factor VIII activity) is required for confirmation, the most likely diagnosis is Hemophilia A.
